items.title: Government of Mozambique, ECA, UNCTAD and the private sector unite to advance green industrialisation in Southern Africa
items.summary: The commitment was underscored during the Workshop on Regional Studies on Innovative Climate Action to Accelerate Green Industrialization in Southern Africa, held in Maputo under the United Nations Development Account (UNDA) 17th Tranche Project. The event brought together government officials, development partners, private sector representatives, academia, and civil society to review regional studies and identify practical pathways to advance green industrial development Opening the workshop, H.E. Custódia Paunde, State Secretary for Industry at Mozambique’s Ministry of Economy, emphasised that industrialisation remains a fundamental national priority and that sustainability should be seen as an opportunity to modernise production systems and enhance competitiveness “Industrialization remains a central, priority and non-negotiable strategic objective in Mozambique’s development agenda.

items.title: Terrorists increasingly targeting civilians in three Cabo Delgado districts – ACLED
items.summary: Maputo, 19 Oct (AIM) – Islamic State Mozambique (ISM) has increasingly targeted civilians in the districts of Mocimboa da Praia, Muidumbe, and Macomia, in the southern Mozambican province of Cabo Delgado over the months of August and September. According to the latest report carried out by the independent conflict registration project ACLED (Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project), the terrorists have been tightening security measures in Mocimboa da Praia, constraining commercial and humanitarian activity. “As a result, the town is likely to become tense. That tension may be directed toward the state, either through protests or increased collaboration with ISM. Evidence suggests that ISM’s return to Nangade is to draw on support from neighboring Tanzania, a development likely to lead to tightened security measures on both sides of the border”, reads the report. Meanwhile, the early October release of hostages taken by ISM in Niassa province last month in return for ransom is likely to embolden the group to target foreigners for abduction in the future.

items.title: Katya Adler: France's government under pressure after weekend of widespread violence
items.summary: President Emmanuel Macron urged calm in a national address following widespread looting and violence France's Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is holding a crisis cabinet meeting on Monday to assess a weekend of violence and looting across the country, in what were some of the worst scenes of public disorder in modern French history Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez tried to hand in his resignation, the Élysée Palace (French President Macron's HQ) announced on Monday morning. But instead, Macron has asked him to examine how to make France's streets safer and to bring the perpetrators of the weekend violence to justice Over half a million mainly peaceful protesters demonstrated on Saturday against rising living costs and dwindling access to decent public services, including a good state education. But the protests turned nasty after groups of black-clad, masked activists and vandals appeared An estimated 1,500 shops and businesses were looted and destroyed. Riot police fired tear gas and turned water cannon on crowds. They were seen hitting people with batons in several places.

items.title: Mozambique: Zero sesame export rejections in the EU and Japan in 2026
items.summary: A total of 6,400 tonnes were exported, of which 1,400 tonnes went to the European Union, across 33 consignments, and 5,000 tonnes to Japan, across 31 consignments Mozambique’s total sesame exports to all destinations during the January-to-September period stood at 48,915 tonnes, with no returns recorded, according to the available data This result was achieved for the first time in the past five years, following the rejection of 14 consignments of Mozambican origin in the two markets over the previous three years By contrast, during the period under review, the European Union recorded 56 rejections of imported sesame and Japan recorded nine, associated with the presence of Salmonella, pesticide residues and aflatoxins Among the countries of origin of the rejected products, Nigeria stood out with 31 cases, followed by India with 12, Sudan with 11 and Tanzania with five, according to data from the European Union’s Rapid Alert System for Food and Feed (RASFF) and Japan’s Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW), covering January to September 2026 The result reflects progress in…

items.title: Deepfakes, bots and distrust: How AI is shaping Israel's election
items.summary: For the first time, AI is playing a major role in Israel's elections. Observers warn that deepfakes, bots and influence campaigns could sway voters In a 19-second clip posted to X, Gadi Eisenkot, a candidate for prime minister, stands with his arms outstretched and a huge smile on his face. In slow motion, he runs through a meadow toward a person who resembles his son, wearing a shirt with the words "Israeli Unity." But Eisenkot sails past him and instead embraces Mansour Abbas, a prominent Arab politician who leads the Ra'am party , running in the elections The video was posted on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's account. Opinion polls show Netanyahu and Eisenkot, who also happens to be a former chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces, in a tight race. The AI-generated video appears to be designed to play on anti-Arab sentiment — a big part of Netanyahu's campaign The clip was viewed more than 1 million times and stirred outrage.
